"Design a foundational prototype and system architecture for a 2D side-scrolling pixel art fantasy Auto-Battler / Management RPG.
CRITICAL GAMEPLAY RULE: The player DOES NOT control the characters in combat. There are NO movement joysticks or manual attack buttons. Characters fight completely automatically against continuous incoming waves of enemies. The player's ONLY role is resource management, squad deployment, and upgrading.
Core Systems @COMMENT_BODY@ Mechanics:
1. Perspective @COMMENT_BODY@ Art Style: 2D Side-scrolling view, using a fantasy pixel art aesthetic. The top half of the screen shows the auto-battle, the bottom half contains the management UI.
2. Class @COMMENT_BODY@ Party System: There are 9 distinct classes: Tank-Warrior, Mage, Archer, Healer-Support, Heavy Tank, Dagger (Assassin), Dark Mage, Xbow (Crossbowman), and Necromancer. The player can deploy a maximum of 4 characters to the battlefield at the same time.
3. Economy @COMMENT_BODY@ Grind Loop: Defeated enemy waves drop equipment and gold. Players can equip these items to their characters or melt/salvage unwanted gear into additional gold. Gold is used to upgrade character skills and base stats.
4. Equipment @COMMENT_BODY@ Rarity System: Gear has levels and a strict color-coded rarity hierarchy. The exact rarity scale from lowest to highest must be: Common -> Uncommon -> Rare -> Epic -> Legendary -> Mythic -> Star -> Moon -> Sun -> Void.
5. UI Requirements: A clean management interface focused on inventory, melting/salvaging items, character selection (deploying the 4-man squad), and skill upgrade menus.\"6. Localization: The entire user interface, skill names, equipment names, rarity labels, and menus must be fully displayed in Turkish.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"
